items.summary: Complex multiplication, coherent addition, and quadratic readout are related ingredients of quantum calculation, but they answer different reconstruction questions. We separate them on a supplied reciprocal carrier. The centralizer of a complex structure on a real two-plane is the complex algebra; its invertible transports are nevertheless not closed under the addition needed for destructive interference at a selected output. A one-outcome dephaser and a reversible phase kick show that certainty of a public outcome does not imply nondisturbance. Within an explicitly assumed positive quadratic response class, calibrated zero-leakage comparisons on a connected tree select the all-ones Gram kernel. We prove quantitative stability estimates and retain the distinction between unconditional record-local operations, selective conditioning, and a controlled inverse interaction. A local normalized-weight ansatz, arbitrary anchored orthogonal refinement, and additive coarse-graining of recorded outcomes force weights proportional to quadratic size. Equal binary refinement alone does not: a positive continuous increasing log-periodic function supplies a counterexample, while binary and ternary refinement at every size, with continuity, recover linearity in size. Real rotations implement the requisite refinements and controlled tagging without full complex control. Fixed-complement preservation and reciprocal reversal admit different generator sectors; independently switchable real mixers on a connected graph plus one addressable local phase generate the unitary Lie algebra. A common scalar phase does not. Supplementary finite action–phase and history examples expose the remaining calibration assumptions. The contribution is an assumption-controlled synthesis of conditional selectors and obstructions, not the introduction of the standard component constructions. The carrier, comparison response, control resources, tensor interpretation, and empirical probability interface are not derived from primitive complementarity.

items.summary: We consider inverse problems for a time-fractional diffusion equation with a second-order elliptic operator and the homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition in a bounded domain of $\mathbb R^N$. The initial value is unknown and is not assumed to be zero. The main result concerns the simultaneous determination of the fractional order and the time-dependent source factor from one weighted spatial observation. For irrational orders in $(0,1)$ and bounded source factors satisfying an exponential integrability condition, we prove that a nonzero observation given for all positive times uniquely determines both unknowns. We also describe the information about the initial value determined by this observation. A counterexample shows that uniqueness of the source factor may fail at the classical order $α=1$, even when the observation is nonzero. In the second part, we establish two uniqueness results for the fractional order when the elliptic operators, initial values, and source terms in the compared equations may be different. The first result is proved by the Laplace transform, whereas the second uses short-time observations and the asymptotic behavior of the Mittag--Leffler functions.
items.title: Uniqueness in determining the temporal source factor and the fractional order with an unknown initial value

items.summary: Language-model agents increasingly improve by converting execution experience into reusable external skills. Yet repeated skill updates form a learning process of their own: locally useful edits can accumulate into redundant or task-specific instructions, while new updates can disrupt behavior that previously worked. We study this problem as skill-evolution overfitting and introduce SkillEvoReg, a general regularization framework for skill evolution inspired by anti-overfitting techniques in neural-network training. SkillEvoReg combines training-time skill dropout, which perturbs update generation, and complexity-aware local regularization, which controls unnecessary structural growth, with causal counterexample validation (CCV), which provides targeted behavioral validation of candidate-specific regressions. We instantiate the framework across heterogeneous skill-evolution systems while retaining each system's native skill evolver and task evaluator. Across SkillOpt, SkillEvolBench, and ContinualSkillBench, SkillEvoReg consistently controls skill-state growth while preserving competitive downstream capability, improves several transfer and later-stage evolution outcomes, and identifies update-level regressions that structural metrics alone cannot reveal. These results suggest that explicit regularization is a useful complement to increasingly capable skill updaters.
items.title: SkillEvoReg: Regularizing Agent Skill Evolution Against Overfitting

items.summary: The Duffin-Schaeffer Conjecture, proven in 2020, gives a zero-full dichotomy for the approximation of irrational numbers with reduced fractions for arbitrary approximation functions. We construct approximation functions such that the inhomogeneous analogue of the Duffin-Schaeffer Conjecture fails. The counterexamples are obtained for all non-zero rationals and certain Liouville numbers.
items.title: Counterexamples to the inhomogeneous Duffin-Schaeffer Conjecture

items.summary: Large language model-based multi-agent debate (MAD) systems are being increasingly used as complex decision pipelines in distributed processes. However, their final synthesis phase still remains inadequately controlled. Even with detailed debate logs, summarizing models are prone to fabricating smoothly written debate consensus that is not grounded in the debate's history. To address this safety gap, this paper presents empirical research and studies if the introduction of active post-debate verification can mitigate the production of such factually unsupported summaries, while still providing valuable information. Furthermore, it is examined whether explicitly signalling divergence is preferable in the absence of a reliable compromise. The Active Provenance Gate (APG) is introduced as a post-debate verification layer that treats the source as a hard constraint, analysing the debate logs, auditing each claim, and applying self-correction. In crisis simulations, the self-healing mechanism more than doubles the average data Provenance Fidelity in difficult condition scenarios, before the strict gate blocks unsupported claims and generates divergence reports. In the human study, a vast majority of the users (over 75%) preferred a report explicitly stating failure in critical scenarios, despite most of them perceiving fabricated consensus from the baseline system as more fluent. Our main contribution is the transition of data origin tracing from passive logging to active conditional blocking before publication.
items.title: Towards Mitigating Fabricated Consensus: The Active Provenance Gate for Multi-Agent Debate Synthesis

items.summary: Gradient-based optimization (GBO) of problems constrained by partial differential equations is central to parameter identification and structural design in solid mechanics. Lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) schemes for linear elastic solids have only recently been derived. Combined with automatically generated discrete adjoint collision kernels, they make GBO possible with a purely LBM-based primal and adjoint solver. We propose, to our knowledge, the first optimization benchmarks for solid LBM: three inverse problems, each with a manufactured solution of the forward problem and a known reference control. These are the identification of two scalar amplitudes of a body force field on a periodic domain, the distributed control of the same field with up to $12800$ degrees of freedom, and the identification of Young's modulus on an elliptic plate with Dirichlet and Neumann boundaries. The primal scheme converges with second order on the periodic domain and with first order on the elliptic plate. The recovered controls follow these rates, with experimental orders of convergence of $1.92$ and $1.06$, respectively. Gradients obtained via forward-mode automatic differentiation (f-AD) and the discrete adjoint LBM (ALBM) require the same number of optimization steps and yield control errors agreeing to at least eleven significant digits. The ALBM gradient is further validated node-wise against a finite difference quotient, with deviations decreasing under mesh refinement. The benchmarks are implemented in the open-source LBM framework OpenLB and provide a verification basis for optimization in LBM-based solid mechanics and its extension to fluid-structure interaction.
items.title: Benchmark cases for gradient-based optimization in linear elastic solid mechanics using lattice Boltzmann methods

items.summary: The rapid development of powered-lift aircraft introduces novel electric propulsion systems lacking established service histories in lightning environments. To ensure flight safety applicants will show compliance with the airworthiness criteria outlined in FAA AC 21.17-4 (Type Certification Powered-Lift). This will ensure that these aircraft are safeguarded against catastrophic vehicle-level effects as well as hazardous or major propeller-level effects resulting from lightning strikes. This paper provides comprehensive guidance for conducting a Lightning Hazard Assessment (LHA) explicitly tailored to powered-lift electric propulsion systems. Applying the methodology outlined in SAE ARP5577 (Aircraft Lightning Direct Effects Certification), this assessment evaluates the direct effects of lightning attachment and current transfer on the structural and mechanical elements of the propulsion unit. By defining a simplified propulsion unit architecture, this paper traces expected current conduction paths from the propulsor blades through the hub, motor shaft, bearings, and motor controller down to the airframe. Furthermore, it details potential failure mechanisms for critical components, including resistive heating and acoustic shock damage in composite blades, arcing and pitting at metallic bearing interfaces, dielectric breakdown of internal motor insulation, and injected transients affecting sensitive power electronics. The assessment also accounts for novel operational scenarios inherent to these vehicles, such as distributed electric propulsion and vectored thrust tilt mechanisms. Ultimately, this paper highlights critical verification strategies—primarily laboratory testing—and continuing airworthiness considerations, such as post-strike inspections, essential for ensuring the long-term safety and reliability of powered-lift electric propulsion systems.
items.title: Guidance for Powered-Lift Electric Propulsion System Lightning Hazard Assessments

items.summary: Efficient acquisition of correlated continuous-time signals is critical in applications such as distributed sensor networks and array processing. However, existing correlation models often fail to capture the shared structure of physical signals measured in close proximity. In this paper, we model each signal in an ensemble as the sum of a hidden common lowpass component and a signal-specific innovation highpass component with disjoint spectral supports, where the common bandwidth is unknown. We first derive theoretical identifiability conditions guaranteeing unique decomposition and reconstruction from subsampled observations. Further, we propose a practical recovery algorithm and a joint reconstruction framework that leverages parametric structured dictionaries parameterized by the unknown common bandwidth. Numerical experiments on an ensemble of four signals demonstrate exact reconstruction with a 25% aggregate sampling rate reduction under identifiability conditions, and robust recovery with up to a 74% rate reduction when all channels are sampled below the Nyquist rate, significantly reducing data acquisition and hardware overhead.
items.title: Identifiability and Joint Recovery of a Structured Signal Ensemble From Sub-Nyquist Samples

The initial value is unknown and is not assumed to be zero. The main result concerns the simultaneous determination of the fractional order and the time-dependent source factor from one weighted spatial observation. For irrational orders in $(0,1)$ and bounded source factors satisfying an exponential integrability condition, we prove that a nonzero observation given for all positive times uniquely determines both unknowns. We also describe the information about the initial value determined by this observation. A counterexample shows that uniqueness of the source factor may fail at the classical order $α=1$, even when the observation is nonzero. In the second part, we establish two uniqueness results for the fractional order when the elliptic operators, initial values, and source terms in the compared equations may be different. The first result is proved by the Laplace transform, whereas the second uses short-time observations and the asymptotic behavior of the Mittag--Leffler functions.
items.title: Uniqueness in determining the temporal source factor and the fractional order with an unknown initial value

items.summary: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) build neural representations of time-dependent PDE solutions, naturally incorporating physics knowledge and observational data, which makes them well suited to both forward and inverse PDE problems. PINNs, however, are known to suffer from spectral bias and lack of causality. Neuro-Spectral Architectures (NeuSA), a recently proposed alternative to PINNs, mitigate both issues, but their numerical integration becomes unstable for stiff differential equations arising in many relevant physical problems. This study proposes Neuro-Spectral Exponential Time Differencing Architectures (NEXT), which combines the spectral representation of the PDE solution in NeuSA with high-order exponential integrators. Within this approach, the linear stiff part of the vector field induced by the PDE is integrated exactly through matrix exponentials, while the possibly nonlinear remainder is modeled by a neural network. The effectiveness of NEXT is verified through benchmark experiments on a set of stiff PDEs, in which NEXT is stable and accurate while NeuSA diverges numerically. It is also shown that NEXT can be applied to inverse problems, where the model has to learn unknown parameters or boundary conditions from sparse data. All code used in this work is publicly available at: https://github.com/marcioh2m/next.git .
items.title: NEXT: Physics-Informed Neuro-Spectral Exponential Time Differencing Architectures

items.summary: Convergence in parameter estimation classically requires ``persistency of excitation," which is a non-degeneracy condition on a trajectory-dependent signal. This paper develops, to the best of our knowledge, the first such excitation theory for a nonlinear partial differential equation. In the context of identifying the unknown viscosity from spectral observations in the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations for incompressible fluids, our excitation condition is computable, verifiable a priori, and sharp with respect to scaling. Our approach employs a data assimilation methodology to account for an unknown initial state and select candidate viscosities by minimizing the loss between the low-mode observations of the fluid velocity and low-mode projection of a nudging-based filter that assimilates these observations. The main novelty of our framework is to distinguish a new functional, $\mathsf{W}$, representing the work done by the filter's associated sensitivity variable on the enstrophy, around which our entire analysis is centered. We show that $\mathsf{W}$ is explicitly comparable to the observability Gramian of the associated Gauss--Newton iteration, and subsequently establish the following dichotomy at every critical point of the observational loss: either $\mathsf{W}$ exceeds a certain threshold, in which case the candidate viscosity obeys an explicit error estimate that depends inversely on $\mathsf{W}$ and the observational density $N$, but directly on the error between initial conditions, or else $\mathsf{W}$ is below the threshold and the observations are quantitatively insensitive to parameter updates in a way that is detectable to the user. Notably, our approach is energy-based, and therefore expected to be adaptable to many other nonlinear dissipative systems.
items.title: Excitation and Identifiability in the 2D Navier-Stokes equations

items.summary: Gradient-based optimization (GBO) of problems constrained by partial differential equations is central to parameter identification and structural design in solid mechanics. Lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) schemes for linear elastic solids have only recently been derived. Combined with automatically generated discrete adjoint collision kernels, they make GBO possible with a purely LBM-based primal and adjoint solver. We propose, to our knowledge, the first optimization benchmarks for solid LBM: three inverse problems, each with a manufactured solution of the forward problem and a known reference control. These are the identification of two scalar amplitudes of a body force field on a periodic domain, the distributed control of the same field with up to $12800$ degrees of freedom, and the identification of Young's modulus on an elliptic plate with Dirichlet and Neumann boundaries. The primal scheme converges with second order on the periodic domain and with first order on the elliptic plate. The recovered controls follow these rates, with experimental orders of convergence of $1.92$ and $1.06$, respectively. Gradients obtained via forward-mode automatic differentiation (f-AD) and the discrete adjoint LBM (ALBM) require the same number of optimization steps and yield control errors agreeing to at least eleven significant digits. The ALBM gradient is further validated node-wise against a finite difference quotient, with deviations decreasing under mesh refinement. The benchmarks are implemented in the open-source LBM framework OpenLB and provide a verification basis for optimization in LBM-based solid mechanics and its extension to fluid-structure interaction.
items.title: Benchmark cases for gradient-based optimization in linear elastic solid mechanics using lattice Boltzmann methods

items.summary: RED-PUMP-2026-v1 is a reproducibility package for a pre-registered fintech-microstructure study of 860,213 pump.fun token launches recorded by an off-chain V3 collector between 2026-05-08 and 2026-06-10 (regime data-collection window). The primary analytical cohort is 749,816 unique mints in the V3 primary window (1,597 GRADUATED, 748,219 TIMEOUT). Two pre-registered analyses are conducted: (i) a measurement audit of the collector's terminal classifier (documented at 04_frozen_inputs/OUTCOME_ASCERTAINMENT_MECHANISM.md); and (ii) a locked temporal-holdout evaluation of a pre-registered logistic association model (15-day development split followed by a 14-day validation split). Of nine automated stability-gate evaluations emitted by the corrected pipeline, two pass, six fail, one is not evaluable. This v1.6 release publishes four frozen protocol documents as redacted copies, with system-specific file paths and identifiers replaced by placeholders, and corrects one input checksum in the pipeline that had stopped the rebuild in earlier versions. Data, outputs and results are unchanged; see REDACTION_NOTE.md. items.summary: Large language model-based multi-agent debate (MAD) systems are being increasingly used as complex decision pipelines in distributed processes. However, their final synthesis phase still remains inadequately controlled. Even with detailed debate logs, summarizing models are prone to fabricating smoothly written debate consensus that is not grounded in the debate's history. To address this safety gap, this paper presents empirical research and studies if the introduction of active post-debate verification can mitigate the production of such factually unsupported summaries, while still providing valuable information. Furthermore, it is examined whether explicitly signalling divergence is preferable in the absence of a reliable compromise. The Active Provenance Gate (APG) is introduced as a post-debate verification layer that treats the source as a hard constraint, analysing the debate logs, auditing each claim, and applying self-correction. In crisis simulations, the self-healing mechanism more than doubles the average data Provenance Fidelity in difficult condition scenarios, before the strict gate blocks unsupported claims and generates divergence reports. In the human study, a vast majority of the users (over 75%) preferred a report explicitly stating failure in critical scenarios, despite most of them perceiving fabricated consensus from the baseline system as more fluent. Our main contribution is the transition of data origin tracing from passive logging to active conditional blocking before publication.
items.title: Towards Mitigating Fabricated Consensus: The Active Provenance Gate for Multi-Agent Debate Synthesis

items.summary: Description (français) : LUMINA est une architecture de traitement de la parole qui prend le signal vocal, et non le texte, comme donnée primaire. Elle met en œuvre le paradigme de l'IA de l'Envers (IA inversée) pour les langues à tradition orale du Maroc : darija, variétés amazighes, arabizi et haketia. Partant du constat que les systèmes généralistes échouent sur ces langues, ce livre blanc soutient que cet échec tient autant aux choix de représentation, de normalisation et de métrique hérités du texte qu'au manque de données. Il propose une formalisation du paradigme en trois inversions et quatre propriétés traduites en hypothèses testables ; une architecture en six couches avec provenance traçable ; cinq métriques d'évaluation communautaires définies formellement ; un modèle de menace propre aux corpus vocaux patrimoniaux ; un cadre de gouvernance opérationnalisant les principes CARE et FAIR ; et un modèle fédéré pour étendre l'approche à d'autres pays du Sud. Description (English, à ajouter dans « Additional descriptions » → Abstract, langue English) : LUMINA is a speech-processing architecture that takes the voice signal, rather than text, as its primary data. It implements the "Inverted AI" paradigm for Morocco's oral-tradition languages: Darija, Amazigh varieties, Arabizi and Haketia. Starting from the observation that general-purpose systems fail on these languages, this white paper argues that the failure stems as much from representation, normalization and evaluation choices inherited from text as from data scarcity. It contributes a formalization of the paradigm as three inversions and four properties translated into testable hypotheses; a six-layer architecture with end-to-end provenance; five formally defined community-centred evaluation metrics; a threat model specific to heritage speech corpora; a governance framework operationalizing the CARE and FAIR principles; and a federated model for extending the approach to other countries of the Global South. items.summary: The Manufacturer Usage Description (MUD) standard allows IoT manufacturers to define expected network behaviors in a MUD file. This file can be translated into enforceable access-control policies, restricting compromised devices to operate solely through manufacturer-defined communication patterns. However, practical adoption of MUD depends on profiles that are accurate, complete, and maintainable. Existing approaches use traffic-based automation but require device deployment and prolonged monitoring, capturing only behavior exercised during observation. Rare, failure-triggered, or configuration-dependent communications may remain absent, producing incomplete policies that disrupt legitimate operation and offer limited insight into the software components responsible for each rule. We present AutoMUD, a source-code-driven tool that generates traceable MUD profiles for IoT devices from their firmware and software source code. AutoMUD combines static and syntactic extraction, retrieval-grounded language-model reasoning, and deterministic validation and compilation to recover the communication behavior characterizing an IoT device and translate eligible endpoints into policy rules. By analyzing code-level evidence, AutoMUD exposes rarely exercised and conditional communication paths, links every generated rule to its source-level provenance, and preserves excluded findings with explicit reasons for review. Our evaluation on a Linux-based repository demonstrates that AutoMUD recovers complete communication behavior, consolidates validated behavior into semantic endpoint groups, and generates structurally valid MUD profiles. Through a controlled semantic fault-injection campaign, we demonstrate that AutoMUD enables analysts to detect, localize, explain, and correct propagated errors, recovering policies semantically identical to their clean counterparts.
items.title: From Source Code to Network Profile: Automated and Traceable MUD Profile Generation for IoT Devices

items.summary: Optimizing embedding systems for production recommendation pipelines demands systematic exploration that consumes disproportionate engineering effort at scale. We apply Andrej Karpathy's AutoResearch paradigm -- a large language model that iteratively edits a training script and retains modifications that improve a held-out scalar metric -- to automate this exploration. We report on twelve weeks of running this paradigm at production scale, where iterations consume hours of multi-GPU compute, evaluation involves competing criteria, and campaigns span weeks across many training jobs. Across two independently developed representation-learning systems for a book recommendation pipeline, we ran 220+ experiments and observed five recurring failure modes absent from the original setting: infrastructure fragility, agent memory decay, search-direction stagnation, iteration-cost asymmetry, and metric fixation. We contribute a three-principle scaffolding design -- prevent, persist, redirect -- that maps each failure mode to a structural remedy and whose instantiation scales with iteration cost. The framework produced a 1.82x Recall@6 lift and a 2.1x coherence lift over hand-tuned baselines, and the agent autonomously designed a text-only fallback that expanded catalog coverage by 5.8x. The two systems span nearly three orders of magnitude in per-iteration cost yet exhibit the same failure modes, suggesting these are structural properties of production-scale autonomous research rather than artifacts of either application.
items.title: AutoResearch at Production Scale: Failure Modes and a Multi-Agent Framework

Contents: the IntentValidator pipeline source snapshot and run configurations; the per-claim datasets of the canonical agent run, of the all-repository human comparison cohort (with its protocol, draw listings and order of events) and of the superseded first human cohort, plus the re-runs that document the effect of the pipeline's timeouts; the 186-pattern NFR claim catalog, boilerplate-stripping rules and the full match table; the extraction-validity ladder and regression scripts; the manual-validation kit (stratified samples, rubric, blind labelling tool, both human raters' sheets with untouched exports and SHA-256 sums, three disclosed LLM annotation passes with per-item rationales and provenance, the LLM-judge sensitivity, the adjudication queue, a recall probe of unflagged pull requests with blind sheets and a disclosed LLM screen, and a kit for a rater from outside the author team); the consistency analysis on the human-validated claims, the Maintainability-Index floor sensitivity and the all-language cross-check of the index against independent Halstead implementations (per-claim results); every analysis script that regenerates the manuscript's numbers and figures; and a checksum manifest of every file with named reproduction checks. The archive carries the replication tree only; the manuscript itself is not included. The AIDev dataset itself is not redistributed; obtain it from its own Zenodo record (10.5281/zenodo.16919272). The 25 September 2026 audit revision adds explicit sampling and interpretation limitations, corrected stratification of diagnostic agreement intervals, clarified nominal instrument coverage, and reproducibility notes. Original human labels and canonical claim verdicts are preserved; catalogue label/rubric conflicts remain for human reassessment. See replication/09-paper/emse-2026/replication/REVIEW-NOTES-2026-09-25.md. Version 2.0.2 (27 September 2026) follows an independent replication of version 2.0.1 from public sources only, which reproduced every result of RQ1–RQ4 and re-ran the pipeline end to end (13.1 % of evaluable agent claims consistent, as published). It adds per-PR provenance (merged flag, P2 membership, measured commits, in-scope files), extraction-tier membership and the multi-metric run's per-metric deltas, a verify mode for the checksum manifest, fixes to the AIDev download script and the manifest's date filter, and clarified requirements and licences. Released runs, labels and generated outputs are unchanged. See replication/09-paper/emse-2026/replication/REVIEW-NOTES-2026-09-27.md.

items.summary: Replication package for the manuscript "Link prediction in complex networks via fusing node centrality and local similarity indices: a fair-protocol reassessment and parameter design principles" (arXiv:2609.09658). It contains all experiment scripts, the locked inputs for the eight real-world networks, the result files underlying every table and figure, and the figure sources. Running python ext_main.py followed by the accompanying scripts (see REPLICATION.md) reproduces the main comparison; python gen_tables.py regenerates the LaTeX tables. Verified in this package: re-running gen_tables.py inside the unpacked archive reproduces tables_generated.tex byte-identically. The degree-corrected benchmark of Sec. 5.7 is reproduced by python aiyappa_degcorr.py. Network data were obtained from public repositories; all processed inputs are included. Environment: Python 3.13 with the pinned dependencies in requirements.txt.

items.summary: Gradient-based optimization (GBO) of problems constrained by partial differential equations is central to parameter identification and structural design in solid mechanics. Lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) schemes for linear elastic solids have only recently been derived. Combined with automatically generated discrete adjoint collision kernels, they make GBO possible with a purely LBM-based primal and adjoint solver. We propose, to our knowledge, the first optimization benchmarks for solid LBM: three inverse problems, each with a manufactured solution of the forward problem and a known reference control. These are the identification of two scalar amplitudes of a body force field on a periodic domain, the distributed control of the same field with up to $12800$ degrees of freedom, and the identification of Young's modulus on an elliptic plate with Dirichlet and Neumann boundaries. The primal scheme converges with second order on the periodic domain and with first order on the elliptic plate. The recovered controls follow these rates, with experimental orders of convergence of $1.92$ and $1.06$, respectively. Gradients obtained via forward-mode automatic differentiation (f-AD) and the discrete adjoint LBM (ALBM) require the same number of optimization steps and yield control errors agreeing to at least eleven significant digits. The ALBM gradient is further validated node-wise against a finite difference quotient, with deviations decreasing under mesh refinement. The benchmarks are implemented in the open-source LBM framework OpenLB and provide a verification basis for optimization in LBM-based solid mechanics and its extension to fluid-structure interaction.
items.title: Benchmark cases for gradient-based optimization in linear elastic solid mechanics using lattice Boltzmann methods

items.summary: Large language model-based multi-agent debate (MAD) systems are being increasingly used as complex decision pipelines in distributed processes. However, their final synthesis phase still remains inadequately controlled. Even with detailed debate logs, summarizing models are prone to fabricating smoothly written debate consensus that is not grounded in the debate's history. To address this safety gap, this paper presents empirical research and studies if the introduction of active post-debate verification can mitigate the production of such factually unsupported summaries, while still providing valuable information. Furthermore, it is examined whether explicitly signalling divergence is preferable in the absence of a reliable compromise. The Active Provenance Gate (APG) is introduced as a post-debate verification layer that treats the source as a hard constraint, analysing the debate logs, auditing each claim, and applying self-correction. In crisis simulations, the self-healing mechanism more than doubles the average data Provenance Fidelity in difficult condition scenarios, before the strict gate blocks unsupported claims and generates divergence reports. In the human study, a vast majority of the users (over 75%) preferred a report explicitly stating failure in critical scenarios, despite most of them perceiving fabricated consensus from the baseline system as more fluent. Our main contribution is the transition of data origin tracing from passive logging to active conditional blocking before publication.
items.title: Towards Mitigating Fabricated Consensus: The Active Provenance Gate for Multi-Agent Debate Synthesis

items.summary: Complex multiplication, coherent addition, and quadratic readout are related ingredients of quantum calculation, but they answer different reconstruction questions. We separate them on a supplied reciprocal carrier. The centralizer of a complex structure on a real two-plane is the complex algebra; its invertible transports are nevertheless not closed under the addition needed for destructive interference at a selected output. A one-outcome dephaser and a reversible phase kick show that certainty of a public outcome does not imply nondisturbance. Within an explicitly assumed positive quadratic response class, calibrated zero-leakage comparisons on a connected tree select the all-ones Gram kernel. We prove quantitative stability estimates and retain the distinction between unconditional record-local operations, selective conditioning, and a controlled inverse interaction. A local normalized-weight ansatz, arbitrary anchored orthogonal refinement, and additive coarse-graining of recorded outcomes force weights proportional to quadratic size. Equal binary refinement alone does not: a positive continuous increasing log-periodic function supplies a counterexample, while binary and ternary refinement at every size, with continuity, recover linearity in size. Real rotations implement the requisite refinements and controlled tagging without full complex control. Fixed-complement preservation and reciprocal reversal admit different generator sectors; independently switchable real mixers on a connected graph plus one addressable local phase generate the unitary Lie algebra. A common scalar phase does not. Supplementary finite action–phase and history examples expose the remaining calibration assumptions. The contribution is an assumption-controlled synthesis of conditional selectors and obstructions, not the introduction of the standard component constructions. The carrier, comparison response, control resources, tensor interpretation, and empirical probability interface are not derived from primitive complementarity.

items.summary: RED-PUMP-2026-v1 is a reproducibility package for a pre-registered fintech-microstructure study of 860,213 pump.fun token launches recorded by an off-chain V3 collector between 2026-05-08 and 2026-06-10 (regime data-collection window). The primary analytical cohort is 749,816 unique mints in the V3 primary window (1,597 GRADUATED, 748,219 TIMEOUT). Two pre-registered analyses are conducted: (i) a measurement audit of the collector's terminal classifier (documented at 04_frozen_inputs/OUTCOME_ASCERTAINMENT_MECHANISM.md); and (ii) a locked temporal-holdout evaluation of a pre-registered logistic association model (15-day development split followed by a 14-day validation split). Development discrimination is strong (AUROC 0.8594); validation discrimination is indistinguishable from chance within the bootstrap interval (AUROC 0.4642, percentile interval [0.4112, 0.5196] containing 0.5000), and validation calibration deteriorates substantially (slope 0.013, intercept +2.816). Of nine automated stability-gate evaluations emitted by the corrected pipeline, two pass, six fail, one is not evaluable. This v1.6 release publishes four frozen protocol documents as redacted copies, with system-specific file paths and identifiers replaced by placeholders, and corrects one input checksum in the pipeline that had stopped the rebuild in earlier versions. Data, outputs and results are unchanged; see REDACTION_NOTE.md. Version 1.5 superseded v1.3 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21908375) per the deposited preprint correction and withdrawal notice at 11_corrigendum/PHASE14_CORRIGENDUM_FOR_ZENODO_21908375.md. The concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20633486 auto-resolves to the latest published version. Package: 72 files (deposit tree plus SHA256SUMS), 348.53 MB. Reproducibility entry point: bash REBUILD_ANALYSIS.sh --launches PATH --outcomes PATH (PowerShell equivalent shipped). Peak resource requirement: approximately 26 GB RAM and 2 hours wall-clock during the 500-replicate day-block bootstrap phase. Frozen input SHA-256 verification is enforced by d1_verify() before execution; internal manifest verifies with sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS (71 files OK). Licenses: manuscript, figures, tables, and provenance documents CC-BY-4.0; code and tests MIT (see LICENSE).

items.summary: Looped transformers reuse weights across recurrence steps, making low-bit quantization especially attractive. We identify two distinct failure modes of standard post-training quantization. On Huginn-3.5B, per-channel INT4 fails primarily at the non-residual loop-entry adapter, while quantizing the residual core is much less damaging. We call this feedback exposure: a quantized layer perturbs the recurrent state without an identity path, and the resulting error is fed back at later steps. Controlled experiments on linear filters and Mamba state-space models show that feedback exposure also occurs outside transformers. Grouped INT4 reveals a separate failure, calibration blindness: our one-step GPTQ baseline builds its Hessian from step-0 activations, leaving input directions used later in the recurrence nearly unweighted. Across nine checkpoints from seven looped architectures, one-step GPTQ is worse than round-to-nearest (RTN) on the primary task metric for five checkpoints. Accumulating the GPTQ Hessian across recurrence steps outperforms both one-step GPTQ and RTN on all nine checkpoints and recovers bf16-level accuracy on Huginn. These results separate two questions for PTQ on looped models: where quantization error enters the recurrence, and which states calibration sees.
items.title: Quantizing Looped Transformers: Feedback Exposure and Calibration Blindness
